entries.name: Replicated Softmax
entries.definition: An undirected document model with binary hidden units and a length-dependent set of categorical word units that share visible-to-hidden weights, with hidden biases scaled by document length.
entries.identity_notes: This is the original Replicated Softmax model of Salakhutdinov and Hinton. It specializes a restricted Boltzmann machine to word-count sufficient statistics across documents of different lengths. It is distinct from repeatedly applying the ordinary softmax function, from the expected-count Constrained Poisson update discussed in the paper, and from the directed deterministic-feature Document NADE architecture. All 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 352 preceding native IDs/names/aliases were compared, with no normalized identity match. Both full-checkout searches included ignored and hidden files; worktree returned 15 lines and main 19. All 16 unique matched contents were read: DocNADE contrasts, frontier and review references, plus four ignored-environment Sage/Pygments entries unrelated to AI SAGE. Twenty-one exact AIO nodes and four complete native neighbors were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Tractable hidden posteriors do not make the partition function or equilibrium model expectation tractable. Finite-step contrastive-divergence updates are not exact maximum-likelihood gradients; deterministic expected counts are not the same as multinomial Gibbs sampling.

The model is conditional on document length and supplies no document-length distribution. Its hidden feature vector has independent conditional Bernoulli coordinates, not topic proportions constrained to sum to one.

For ordinary counting measure on K^D ordered word assignments and F binary hidden units, the zero-weight, zero-bias partition is K^D times 2^F. The AIS discussion’s printed Z_0=2^F needs a corresponding normalized base-measure convention or visible-state factor; it is not adopted unchanged as that counting-measure partition. This is a mathematical qualification of the displayed derivation, not a claim about author-code behavior.
No convergence, topic quality or benchmark advantage is asserted. The later experimental pages and author software were not audited.

claims.statement: For a document with D word positions, vocabulary counts n_k and binary hidden states h_j, use energy E(V,h)=-sum_jk W_jk h_j n_k-sum_k b_k n_k-D sum_j a_j h_j. The joint probability is proportional to exp(-E) with a partition function for that length. Hidden units are conditionally independent given words, with P(h_j=1|V)=sigmoid(D a_j+sum_k W_jk n_k). Given h, positions independently draw words from softmax(b_k+sum_j W_jk h_j); equivalently, sample D word counts from the corresponding multinomial. Parameter sharing makes the ordered-word probability permutation invariant. A count-vector probability includes the number of distinct ordered realizations. Learning contrasts data and model sufficient statistics; the paper approximates the model term with finite alternating Gibbs steps initialized at data.

entries.name: Sparse additive generative model
entries.definition: A generative model family for categorical text data that forms word probabilities by normalizing a background log-frequency vector plus sparse component deviations, allowing multiple generative facets to combine additively in log space.
entries.identity_notes: SAGE here denotes Eisenstein, Ahmed and Xing’s sparse additive generative construction, not Sage mathematical software or graph-neural aggregation. Its classification, topic and multifaceted uses share this parameterization; it is not synonymous with all naive Bayes models, sparse dictionary learning, sparse topic proportions or an arithmetic mixture of component word distributions. All 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 352 preceding native IDs/names/aliases were compared, with no normalized identity match. Both full-checkout searches included ignored and hidden files; worktree returned 15 lines and main 19. All 16 unique matched contents were read: DocNADE contrasts, frontier and review references, plus four ignored-environment Sage/Pygments entries unrelated to AI SAGE. Twenty-one exact AIO nodes and four complete native neighbors were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: Sparsity concerns log deviations. Finite logits still give positive word probabilities, and even zero-deviation words can change absolute probability through normalization; their relative odds remain those of the background when their deviations agree.

Additive log facets yield multiplicative unnormalized effects, not an arithmetic probability mixture. The model family does not require every document to have a single observed class or prohibit latent variables.

The Jeffreys-prior paragraph on PDF p.4 prints expected inverse variance equal to eta squared. Its preceding Gamma moment and b=eta squared/(a-1) instead give 1/eta squared for nonzero eta, with a>1 and positive scale. The printed final identity is not adopted; zero deviations require a limiting/numerical treatment. The improper prior is not represented as a normalized marginal distribution.

The paper warns that warm-starting tightly coupled deviation/variance updates can lock in early sparsity patterns. Neither approximate inference nor Newton updates establish global convergence or calibrated posterior uncertainty.

The single-component rank-one Hessian argument is not asserted unchanged for sums over multiple facet combinations. No author implementation, universal predictive advantage or numerical benchmark result is certified.

claims.statement: For a component k, set p(w=i|k) proportional to exp(m_i+eta_ki), normalizing over the vocabulary. Multiple selected facets contribute a sum of their deviation vectors before this normalization; no additional token-level switch is needed to choose which facet generates the word. This does not remove latent topic assignments used by a topic-model variant. The paper places sparsity-inducing priors on deviations, using zero-mean Gaussian components with latent variances: an exponential variance prior gives a Laplace marginal, while an alternative improper Jeffreys prior gives a different shrinkage construction. It combines MAP estimates of deviations with variational treatment of other latent quantities. For a single component and fixed expected precisions, the gradient is observed or expected counts minus total count times word probabilities minus the precision-weighted deviations; its Hessian is a rank-one term minus a diagonal term, enabling the reported efficient Newton update.

entries.name: Hierarchical softmax
entries.definition: A neural categorical-output component that assigns a probability to each vocabulary leaf by multiplying normalized branch probabilities along its path through a word tree.
entries.identity_notes: This record covers the hierarchical probability output component, including the binary sigmoid form described as hierarchical softmax by Mikolov and colleagues. Morin and Bengio’s parameter-sharing language model and Mnih and Hinton’s hierarchical log-bilinear model are complete architectures using this factorization, not aliases for the component. A Huffman tree, a WordNet-derived tree and a learned tree are construction choices with different scope. All 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 352 preceding native IDs/names/aliases were compared, with no normalized identity match. Both full-checkout searches included ignored and hidden files; worktree returned 15 lines and main 19. All 16 unique matched contents were read: DocNADE contrasts, frontier and review references, plus four ignored-environment Sage/Pygments entries unrelated to AI SAGE. Twenty-one exact AIO nodes and four complete native neighbors were inspected. Absence is bounded to this snapshot and semantic neighborhood.
limitations: The tree parameterization defines a normalized distribution of its own. Calling it an approximation to full softmax does not assert equality to probabilities from a particular flat-softmax parameter set or provide a numerical approximation-error bound.

Logarithmic target cost requires suitable depth or weighted-average code length. A full binary tree alone can have linear worst-case depth. Even a Huffman code’s mean length need not be at most log2(vocabulary size): three equally frequent words have optimal mean length 5/3, exceeding log2(3). Thus the unqualified average-length sentence in Mikolov Section 2.1 is not adopted as a universal bound.
Computing every vocabulary probability requires at least linear output work. The short-path calculation does not by itself give a logarithmic-time exact top-k or most-probable-word search.

Shared internal nodes, tree construction and input representation constrain the fitted model. Multiple codes per word add paths and require their sum, rather than selecting an arbitrary single leaf or averaging leaf probabilities.

This component is not a whole language model, a hard decision tree, negative sampling, or Gumbel-Softmax sampling. No empirical speedup, embedding-quality ranking or author-code behavior is certified.

claims.statement: In a binary tree with one leaf per word, each internal node computes a branch probability from the input representation, commonly sigmoid of a node-vector dot product with optional bias. The opposite branch has its complement. Multiply the appropriate branch probabilities on the target word’s path to obtain its exact probability under this tree-parameterized distribution; probabilities over all leaves sum to one. The negative log probability is a sum of binary losses, so only nodes on the observed path contribute output-parameter gradients. For a sigmoid node logit and branch indicator y, that loss derivative is sigmoid(logit)-y. Computing one target probability and its gradient costs work proportional to its path length, in addition to representation computation. The source’s skip-gram variant uses internal-node output vectors and frequency-based Huffman codes. Multiple leaves assigned to one word require summing their disjoint path probabilities, as in the HLBL extension.

limitations: Pathwise gradients can be unbiased for the specified continuous relaxed objective under regularity conditions while remaining biased for the original discrete objective. A correct categorical argmax law does not make the relaxed gradient an unbiased discrete-gradient estimator.

Temperature zero is a limit, not a valid value in the softmax division. Small temperatures can produce sharp derivatives and difficult variance or numerical behavior; no universally optimal temperature or annealing schedule is asserted.
The positive-weight construction excludes zero-mass categories or requires a declared limiting representation. Finite-precision softmax, noise endpoints and ties require numerical policies.
A uniform vector at very high temperature is different from a uniform probability density across the simplex. The relaxation is not generally a Dirichlet distribution.

Distributional equivalence does not imply equivalence of training losses. When a variational objective includes latent log probabilities, replacing discrete states by soft values without a consistent density treatment need not preserve a lower bound for the intended discrete model.

A downstream objective must be defined on the continuous simplex for relaxed training. A model may exploit interior values and suffer a gap when later evaluated with discrete states; neither task quality nor unbiased discrete optimization is guaranteed.

claims.statement: For n≥2 categories with positive finite weights alpha_i and temperature tau>0, draw independent standard Gumbel G_i and set y_i=exp((log(alpha_i)+G_i)/tau) divided by the sum of those exponentials. Normalizing alpha beforehand only adds a common log shift and leaves y unchanged. Each draw has positive components summing to one and is differentiable in the log weights at positive temperature. Holding the base noise fixed allows the chain rule to estimate gradients of a differentiable objective evaluated on this relaxed random vector, under the usual conditions permitting differentiation under expectation. Argmax rounding has categorical probabilities alpha_i/sum(alpha) for every positive temperature; using the same noise while tau tends to zero yields the corresponding one-hot sample almost surely. For fixed finite perturbed scores, tau tending to infinity yields the uniform vector. The relaxed vector at finite temperature is not itself a categorical one-hot draw.

claims.statement: Draw independent Gumbel noise and compute y=softmax((log(alpha)+G)/tau) with positive finite weights and tau>0. In the forward pass, use z as the one-hot vector at argmax(y), equivalently argmax(log(alpha)+G). In the backward pass, approximate the derivative of z with respect to its parameters by the derivative of y, while the downstream computation has received z. Thus the downstream gradient evaluated at the hard forward state is multiplied by the relaxed sample’s Jacobian. For log-weight coordinates ell and fixed noise/temperature, that Jacobian has entries y_i(delta_ij−y_j)/tau. Hard output remains one-hot even at large positive temperature, and its categorical sampling law is independent of tau; temperature changes the backward surrogate. This is a deliberately biased surrogate, not the ordinary derivative of the hard argmax or generally the gradient obtained by evaluating the whole loss on y.

limitations: Order invariance of the summed document representation does not imply exchangeability of the sequence likelihood. The symmetrized probability of each sequence differs from its count-vector probability by the number of distinct permutations; duplicate words change that number.

For a word whose tree path has length L, conditional output work is O(HL). The claimed logarithmic vocabulary scaling requires suitable tree depth or average depth; a full binary tree alone can have linear depth. The record does not assert a logarithmic worst case for every full tree.

The main paper’s text below Equation (11) retains vi=1 in the joint product although words are categorical. The curated likelihood uses the observed word and its branch path, consistent with Equations (9) and (11) and the supplement’s probability computation.

For Bernoulli tree training, the negative-log-likelihood derivative is the probability of the right branch minus the observed branch indicator. The supplement’s p(actual branch)-indicator notation must not be read literally as the probability of the observed left branch when that indicator is zero. No author implementation behavior is inferred.

The stated model is conditional on document length and does not supply a learned document-length distribution. Shared additive prefix features discard order within the observed prefix. Hidden topic features are deterministic representations, not posterior latent-topic probabilities.
No classification/retrieval advantage, semantic quality guarantee, exact symmetrized-mixture training gradient or implementation certification is asserted.

claims.statement: For a document of given length D, form h_i=sigmoid(c+sum_(k<i) W[:,v_k]); the same word embedding and output parameters are reused across positions, and the preactivation is updated by adding the newly observed word’s embedding. A flat softmax can normalize the next-word distribution. The paper’s final model replaces it with a binary tree whose leaves are vocabulary words: each internal node predicts the probability of taking its right branch, and a word probability is the product of its observed left/right branch probabilities. Multiply all observed-word conditionals to obtain a normalized probability over length-D sequences. Train by differentiating their negative log likelihood. After all words, h(v)=sigmoid(c+sum_i W[:,v_i]) is an order-invariant document representation; tanh is also tested. For count-vector input, the paper samples word occurrences without replacement to produce uniformly random distinct orderings and trains on those sequences. Its separate symmetrized sequence model averages probabilities over distinct permutations; training on sampled order log losses is a surrogate for that log mixture. A count-vector probability instead sums the unsymmetrized sequence probabilities over its distinct permutations.

source_analysis.mapping_assessment: All 241 semantic label/scoped-synonym hits were read, followed by 21 complete CLASS nodes with annotations and outgoing edges and 4 full native neighbors. Replicated Softmax broadly maps to RestrictedBoltzmannMachine and relates to the task-scoped ProbabilisticTopicModel. SAGE relates to ProbabilisticTopicModel because topic modeling is an explicit use, while observed-class and multifaceted generative models extend beyond that task. SparseLearning is dictionary learning, SparseAutoEncoder concerns hidden activity, and SparseLLM concerns compression; these are not SAGE identities. Hierarchical softmax broadly maps to OutputLayer.
